drugs.name: Bethanechol

fields.drug: Bethanechol. Also listed as Bethanecol in chart. Direct muscarinic agonist.
fields.action: Stimulates muscarinic receptors, increasing bladder detrusor contraction and gastrointestinal motility.
fields.dosage:
FORMS / STRENGTHS
Oral tablets: 5, 10, 25, 50 mg.
DOSE / SCOPE
Adult nonobstructive urinary retention: 10-50 mg orally 3-4 times daily; individualized to response.
fields.indication: Postoperative/postpartum nonobstructive urinary retention; neurogenic bladder atony.
fields.contraindication: Hypersensitivity; hyperthyroidism; peptic ulcer; latent or active asthma; pronounced bradycardia or hypotension; vasomotor instability; coronary artery disease; epilepsy or parkinsonism. Do not use with mechanical GI/urinary obstruction or when contraction may harm recent surgery or a weakened wall; consult the product label for the complete exclusions.
fields.adverse: Bronchospasm, marked bradycardia or hypotension; cholinergic toxicity.
fields.effects: Abdominal cramps, diarrhea, salivation, sweating, flushing, nausea.
fields.notes: Take on an empty stomach. Confirm retention is not due to obstruction.

fields.action: Activates muscle nicotinic receptors and maintains depolarization, causing transient fasciculation followed by paralysis.
fields.dosage:
FORMS / STRENGTHS
Injection example: 20 mg/mL.
DOSE / SCOPE
Adult short-procedure/intubation label: average 0.6 mg/kg IV; specialist anesthetic and airway management required.
fields.indication: Facilitation of tracheal intubation; skeletal-muscle relaxation during anesthesia.
fields.contraindication: Malignant-hyperthermia susceptibility, skeletal myopathy, hypersensitivity; after acute phase of major burns, trauma, denervation or upper motor-neuron injury.

fields.effects: Fasciculations, postoperative muscle pain, transient bradycardia.
fields.notes: Paralysis is NOT sedation or pain relief. Requires ventilation/anesthesia. Plasma cholinesterase deficiency can prolong paralysis.

fields.drug: Sildenafil citrate. Examples: Viagra for erectile dysfunction (ED); Revatio for pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH). Different uses require different regimens.

fields.dosage:

- Revatio: 20 mg oral tablets; oral suspension 10 mg/mL after reconstitution; injection 10 mg/12.5 mL (0.8 mg/mL).

- ED: 50 mg orally as needed about 1 hour before sex (30 minutes to 4 hours beforehand); adjust to 25-100 mg. Maximum once daily.
- PAH: 20 mg orally three times daily. The current Revatio label permits specialist titration up to 80 mg three times daily. IV: 10 mg three times daily under clinical care. These are not interchangeable ED doses.
fields.indication: ED in adult men (Viagra). PAH, WHO Group I, to improve exercise ability and delay clinical worsening in adults (Revatio). Revatio also has a pediatric indication; pediatric dosing is outside this adult summary.
fields.contraindication: Organic nitrates or nitric-oxide donors, including recreational nitrites; riociguat; known hypersensitivity to sildenafil or formulation ingredients.
fields.adverse:
- Severe hypotension or fainting; prolonged erection / priapism; reports of sudden vision loss (including NAION) or sudden hearing loss.
- An erection lasting over 4 hours needs emergency care; sudden vision or hearing changes need urgent assessment.
fields.effects: Headache, flushing, indigestion, nasal congestion, dizziness and transient visual/color changes. PAH treatment may also cause diarrhea, muscle pain or nosebleeds.
fields.notes:
- Half-life is about 4 hours. A high-fat meal can delay absorption.
- ED: consider a 25 mg start with age over 65, liver impairment, severe renal impairment or interacting medicines. Ritonavir: no more than 25 mg in 48 hours. Alpha-blockers can add hypotension risk.
- Do not combine with another PDE5 inhibitor or another sildenafil product. ED use is inappropriate when sexual activity is medically inadvisable; assess cardiovascular risk.

Adult selected arrhythmias with suitable renal function: initial 80 mg twice daily. Renal-adjusted intervals and QT-based titration are mandatory.
fields.indication: Life-threatening ventricular arrhythmias; maintenance of sinus rhythm in selected symptomatic AF/flutter.
fields.contraindication: Long-QT syndrome, potassium below 4 mEq/L, asthma, major bradycardia/AV block, shock/decompensated failure; additional AF QT/renal restrictions apply.
fields.adverse: Torsades, severe bradycardia, heart block, bronchospasm and heart failure.
fields.effects: Fatigue, dizziness, dyspnea, nausea.
fields.notes: Initiate/reinitiate in a resuscitation-capable facility with continuous ECG, ordinarily at least 3 days. Correct electrolytes; calculate creatinine clearance.

fields.action: Prolongs cardiac action potentials, partly through a slow inward current, facilitating rhythm conversion.
fields.dosage:
FORMS / STRENGTHS
Injection: 0.1 mg/mL, commonly 1 mg/10 mL vial.
DOSE / SCOPE
Adult recent-onset AF/flutter: at least 60 kg, 1 mg IV over 10 minutes; below 60 kg, 0.01 mg/kg over 10 minutes. Further dose only per monitored protocol.
fields.indication: Rapid conversion of recent-onset atrial fibrillation/flutter to sinus rhythm.
fields.contraindication: Hypersensitivity. Prolonged QT, low potassium/magnesium and significant LV dysfunction increase risk and require careful selection.
fields.adverse: Sustained polymorphic VT/torsades, other ventricular arrhythmia and hypotension.
fields.effects: Headache, nausea, transient rhythm changes.
fields.notes: Correct electrolytes; continuous ECG for at least 4 hours or until QT returns to baseline. Defibrillation/resuscitation must be available.

Oral capsules: 125, 250, 500 micrograms.
DOSE / SCOPE
Adult AF/flutter initiation: creatinine clearance above 60 mL/min, 500 micrograms twice daily; 40-60, 250 twice daily; 20 to below 40, 125 twice daily. QT-based reduction is required.
fields.indication: Conversion/maintenance of sinus rhythm in selected AF/flutter.
fields.contraindication: Long-QT or excessive baseline QT; creatinine clearance below 20; interacting drugs including verapamil, cimetidine, trimethoprim, ketoconazole and hydrochlorothiazide.
fields.adverse: Torsades and other life-threatening ventricular arrhythmia.
fields.effects: Headache, dizziness, chest discomfort.
fields.notes: Hospital initiation/reinitiation with continuous ECG for at least 3 days. Check the complete interaction list; micrograms are not milligrams.

fields.action: Restores potassium needed for membrane potential, conduction and normal muscle function.
fields.dosage:
FORMS / STRENGTHS
Example oral potassium chloride ER: 10 or 20 mEq per tablet. State the salt and mEq, not an unspecified mass of potassium.
DOSE / SCOPE
Adult hypokalemia, reviewed oral product: typically 40-100 mEq/day divided; no more than 20 mEq per dose. Adjust to labs and renal function.
fields.indication: Treatment/prevention of hypokalemia; correction can reduce electrolyte-related arrhythmia risk.
fields.contraindication: Hyperkalemia or conditions preventing adequate excretion; concurrent potassium-sparing agents/product-specific GI restrictions require review.
fields.adverse: Life-threatening hyperkalemia/cardiac arrest, GI ulceration or bleeding with solid formulations.
fields.effects: Nausea, vomiting, abdominal discomfort, diarrhea.
fields.notes: Take with meals and water. Check potassium/kidneys. Concentrated IV potassium must NEVER be given by IV push; IV replacement is a separate monitored protocol.

fields.drug: Magnesium. Also listed as Magnesium ion; Mg2+. Electrolyte replacement / membrane stabilizer.
fields.action: Restores magnesium-dependent enzyme and ion-channel functions; affects neuromuscular transmission and cardiac excitability.
fields.dosage:
FORMS / STRENGTHS
Magnesium sulfate injection: 50% (500 mg/mL). IV solutions require dilution to 20% or less. Oral salts differ in elemental content.
DOSE / SCOPE
Reviewed label, adult mild deficiency: 1 g IM every 6 hours for four doses. This is a product-label example, not a universal regimen. Adjust to labs, kidney function and route; eclampsia and arrhythmia regimens differ.
fields.indication: Magnesium deficiency; selected products prevent/treat eclamptic seizures. Monitored protocols also use magnesium for torsades.
fields.contraindication: Heart block or myocardial damage in reviewed injection labeling; severe renal impairment greatly increases toxicity risk.
fields.adverse: Hypermagnesemia, respiratory depression, loss of reflexes, severe hypotension and cardiac arrest.
fields.effects: Flushing, sweating, nausea; oral salts commonly cause diarrhea.
fields.notes: Monitor magnesium, kidney function, respirations and reflexes. Grams of magnesium sulfate do not equal grams of elemental magnesium.
